```{r setup, include = FALSE}

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
for (f in list.files("R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
P <- params
T_YR <- P$time_yr
pct <- function(x, acc = 0.1) ifelse(is.na(x), "-", scales::percent(x, acc))
num <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, digits = d, format = "f")
JOINT_NAME <- c(ANKLE = "Total ankle", ELBOW = "Total elbow")
METHOD_NAME <- c(normal = "Wald (normal approximation)", exact = "exact binomial")
save_fig <- function(p, slug, width = 11, height = 6) if (isTRUE(P$save_png))
  save_plot(p, paste0("metafor_", slug), P$out_dir, width = width, height = height)
SC <- ma_scale(P$ma_scale)
SCN <- P$ma_scale                                   # short name for column labels
SC_OTHER <- setdiff(names(MA_SCALES), P$ma_scale)[1]
src <- function(txt) cat("\n\n<p style='font-size:90%;color:#555'><b>Source:</b> ", txt, "</p>\n\n", sep = "")
```

# Purpose

The rare-joint registries list few models: 4–13 per registry for total ankle and total elbow, and the largest model often holds 30–50% of all procedures. With so few models, a model with a high revision rate pulls the registry mean up and can hide itself and other poor performers from a funnel plot. This report uses a **random-effects meta-analysis** of the model rates (`metafor` package), with **leave-one-out** refits, to:

1. find the models that drive the registry mean;
2. obtain the **least upward-biased mean**, the lowest leave-one-out mean, as an alternative funnel reference; and
3. show how the outliers identified change from the published mean to that mean, at the **90%** and **95%** control limits, with Wald and exact binomial limits compared.

It is a focused version of `loo_influence.Rmd`, limited to the metafor (random-effects) methods. The subtraction-based leave-one-out is left out here. The [summary](#summary) at the end gives the answers in one place.

## Which outputs come from metafor {#metafor-outputs}

| Output | Section | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Meta-analysis summary table (pooled mean, CI, prediction interval, τ², I², Q) | [Random-effects meta-analysis](#re) | **metafor**: `rma()`, `predict()` |
| Weights table | [Random-effects meta-analysis](#re) | **metafor**: `weights()` |
| Forest plot, metafor style | [Random-effects meta-analysis](#re) | **metafor**: `forest()` (native metafor plot) |
| Forest plot, report style | [Random-effects meta-analysis](#re) | **metafor** results (`rma()`, `predict()`), drawn with ggplot2 |
| Leave-one-out table and plot | [Leave-one-out](#loo) | **metafor**: `leave1out()`; plot drawn with ggplot2 |
| Leave-one-out summary across years | [Leave-one-out](#loo) | **metafor**: `rma()`, `leave1out()` |
| Influence table | [Influence diagnostics](#influence) | **metafor**: `influence()` |
| Influence panels | [Influence diagnostics](#influence) | **metafor**: `plot(influence())` (native metafor plot) |
| Cook's distance plot | [Influence diagnostics](#influence) | **metafor**: `influence()`, drawn with ggplot2 |
| Standardised residual plot | [Standardised residuals](#rstudent) | **metafor**: `influence()` (`rstudent`), drawn with ggplot2 |
| Wald vs exact limits (calibration table, plot, status table) | [Control limits](#limits) | Not metafor: binomial calculations in `R/limits.R` |
| 90% and 95% funnels, power table, counts | [90% and 95% limits](#screening) | Funnels are not metafor. Their second reference (lowest leave-one-out mean) **comes from metafor** `leave1out()` |
| Scale sensitivity table (cloglog vs logit) | [Sensitivity](#scale-sensitivity) | **metafor**: `rma()`, `leave1out()` refitted on each scale |
| Summary tables | [Summary](#summary) | metafor `influence()` and `leave1out()`, plus funnel limits from `R/limits.R` |

# Data and model inputs {#data}

```{r load}
cfg <- load_rare_config(".")
exts <- purrr::compact(purrr::map(stats::setNames(unlist(P$joints), unlist(P$joints)), ~ load_rare(P$data_dir, .x)))
runs <- purrr::compact(purrr::map(exts, ~ loo_run(.x, cfg, T_YR, k_min = P$k_min, test = P$ma_test, scale = P$ma_scale)))
skipped <- purrr::imap_chr(runs, ~ paste(.x$skipped, collapse = ", "))
```

**Models.** These are the model rows used by the rare-joint funnels: AOANJRR supplements (A15 ankle, ET6–ET8 elbow) and NJR (3.A4 ankle, 3.E8 elbow). Registries with fewer than `r P$k_min` models are left out: `r paste(sprintf("%s: %s", names(skipped), ifelse(skipped == "", "none", skipped)), collapse = "; ")`. LROI publishes no model-level rates for these joints.

**Input to the meta-analysis.** For each model $i$, the meta-analysis needs an estimate and its variance:

* The estimate is the published Kaplan-Meier cumulative revision rate $p_i$ on a transformed scale, $y_i = f(p_i)$. This report uses the **`r SC$label`** scale (parameter `ma_scale`).
* The standard error comes from the published 95% CI on the same scale, $SE_i = [f(ucl_i) - f(lcl_i)] / (2 \times 1.96)$, and $v_i = SE_i^2$.
* Every pooled result (means, CIs, prediction intervals, leave-one-out means) is **back-transformed** to the proportion scale with $f^{-1}$ before it is shown.

| Scale | $f(p)$ | Back-transform $f^{-1}(y)$ | Delta-method factor $f'(p)$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Complementary log-log (primary) | $\log(-\log(1 - p)) = \log(-\log S)$ | $1 - \exp(-\exp(y))$ | $1 / [-(1-p)\log(1-p)]$ |
| Logit (sensitivity) | $\log(p / (1 - p))$ | $1 / (1 + e^{-y})$ | $1 / [p(1-p)]$ |

**Why the complementary log-log scale.** Registries compute Kaplan-Meier CIs on the log(−log) scale of survival (Kalbfleisch & Prentice 2002; the default in SAS and the approach recommended by the International Prosthesis Benchmarking Working Group 2018). For the published CIs used here, the upper and lower half-widths are symmetric on that scale (median ratio ≈ 1.00), so the SE read back from the CI is the one the registry computed. On another scale the CI is slightly asymmetric and the SE is an approximation. The cloglog scale is also the scale of a proportional-hazards contrast between survival curves, and it was used for pooling arthroplasty survival estimates with REML in `metafor` by Heaps et al. (2019). The logit scale is the usual choice for pooling simple proportions (Lin & Chu 2020; e.g. Greco et al. 2026). When event probabilities are low, as for most revision rates here, the two scales give almost the same answers (Salika et al. 2022), which the [sensitivity analysis](#scale-sensitivity) checks.

Using the published CI rather than a binomial variance from $n$ means the variance allows for censoring and the number still at risk. Both scales keep pooled rates between 0 and 1.

AOANJRR elbow stems are printed separately for fracture, OA and RA. Each stem is pooled into one row: the rate is n-weighted, the SE is combined from the per-diagnosis CIs on the proportion scale, and it is moved to the analysis scale with the delta method, $SE_y = SE_p \times f'(p)$.

```{r inputs}
purrr::map_dfr(runs, "models") |>
  arrange(joint, registry, desc(n_total)) |>
  transmute(joint = JOINT_NAME[joint], registry, model, n = scales::comma(n_total),
            `share of registry n` = pct(share_n), rate = pct(p),
            `95% CI` = ifelse(is.na(lcl), sprintf("%s-%s", pct(SC$inv(yi - 1.96 * sei)), pct(SC$inv(yi + 1.96 * sei))),
                              sprintf("%s-%s", pct(lcl), pct(ucl))),
            y = num(yi, 3), SE = num(sei, 3), `SE source` = se_source) |>
  rename(!!paste0("y (", SCN, ")") := y, !!paste0("SE (", SCN, ")") := SE) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Model inputs at ", T_YR, " years"))
```

# Random-effects meta-analysis {#re}

**Method.** `metafor::rma(yi, vi, method = "REML", test = "knha")` fits

$$y_i = \mu + u_i + e_i, \qquad u_i \sim N(0, \tau^2), \quad e_i \sim N(0, v_i)$$

* $\mu$ is the pooled rate on the `r SC$label` scale. Back-transformed, it is the expected revision rate of a typical **model**.
* $\tau^2$ is the variance of the models' true rates, estimated by REML.
* Each model gets weight $w_i = 1/(v_i + \tau^2)$. When models differ a lot (large $\tau^2$), the weights move towards equal, so a model with 45% of the procedures cannot dominate the mean the way it dominates an n-weighted or published mean.
* The CI of $\mu$ uses the **Knapp-Hartung** adjustment ($t_{k-1}$ with a rescaled variance), which has better coverage than z-based CIs when there are only 4–13 models (IntHout et al. 2014).

**Metrics.**

| Metric | Meaning |
|---|---|
| RE mean (95% CI) | Pooled rate of a typical model, back-transformed from the `r SC$label` scale |
| 95% prediction interval | Range expected for the rate of a new, typical model. It includes $\tau^2$, so it is wider than the CI |
| $\tau^2$ | Between-model variance (`r SC$label` scale, so not comparable across scales). 0 means models differ only by chance |
| $I^2$ | Share of total variation that is between-model rather than sampling error. Roughly 25 / 50 / 75% = low / moderate / high |
| $Q$ (p) | Cochran's test that all models share one rate. It has low power with few models |
| Weight | `weights()`: each model's share of the inverse-variance weight |

```{r re_summary}
purrr::map_dfr(runs, "summary") |>
  transmute(joint = JOINT_NAME[joint], registry, k,
            `published mean (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", pct(p_pub, 0.01), pct(p_lcl), pct(p_ucl)),
            `RE mean (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", pct(p_re, 0.01), pct(p_re_lb), pct(p_re_ub)),
            `95% prediction interval` = sprintf("%s-%s", pct(pi_lb), pct(pi_ub)),
            tau2 = num(tau2, 3), I2 = paste0(round(I2), "%"), Q = sprintf("%.1f (p = %.3f)", QE, QEp)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Random-effects meta-analysis at ", T_YR, " years (metafor rma, predict)"))
```

```{r weights}
purrr::map_dfr(runs, "models") |>
  arrange(joint, registry, desc(n_total)) |>
  transmute(joint = JOINT_NAME[joint], registry, model, `share of n` = pct(share_n, 1),
            `weight, common effect` = pct(w_ce, 1), `weight, random effects` = pct(w_re, 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Share of procedures vs share of weight (metafor weights)")
```

Read the weights table across a row. A random-effects weight below the share of n means the meta-analysis limits that model's pull on the mean. The common-effect weights, from an inverse-variance fit without $\tau^2$, show how strongly a large, precise model would drive the mean otherwise.

## Forest plots

### metafor style

```{r forest_native, results = "asis", fig.width = 9}
for (j in names(runs)) for (r in names(runs[[j]]$fits)) {
  f <- runs[[j]]$fits[[r]]
  k <- f$re$k
  cat("\n\n#### ", JOINT_NAME[[j]], ", ", r, "\n\n", sep = "")
  par(mar = c(4, 0, 1, 0))
  metafor::forest(f$re, transf = function(x) SC$inv(x) * 100, addpred = TRUE, refline = f$summary$p_pub * 100,
                  header = c("Model", paste0(T_YR, "-yr revision % [95% CI]")), xlab = "Cumulative revision (%)",
                  digits = 1, cex = 0.85)
  src("<b>metafor output</b>: <code>forest(rma())</code>. Squares: models (size ~ weight). Diamond: RE mean (95% CI). Dotted line under the diamond: 95% prediction interval. Vertical line: published registry mean.")
}
```

### Report style

```{r forest_gg, results = "asis", fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5.5}
for (j in names(runs)) {
  cat("\n\n#### ", JOINT_NAME[[j]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- plot_loo_forest(runs[[j]], title = paste0(JOINT_NAME[[j]], ", ", T_YR, "-year revision by model"),
         subtitle = "Black: published mean. Blue: random-effects mean (band = 95% CI, dotted = 95% prediction interval). Box size ~ n",
         caption = "Orange boxes: influential by metafor's rule (Viechtbauer & Cheung 2010).")
  print(p); save_fig(p, paste0(tolower(j), "_", T_YR, "yr_forest"), 11, 5.5)
  src("<b>metafor results</b> (<code>rma()</code>, <code>predict()</code>, <code>influence()</code>) drawn with ggplot2.")
}
```

# Leave-one-out {#loo}

**Method.** `metafor::leave1out()` refits the random-effects model $k$ times, each time without one model, and returns the pooled mean (with its CI, $\tau^2$ and $I^2$) without that model. The change from the full RE mean shows how much that model drives the mean.

* A model with a **high** rate that drives the mean **lowers** it when left out.
* The **lowest** leave-one-out mean is the mean without the model that inflates it most. It is the **least upward-biased** mean available (supervisor guidance) and is used below as the alternative funnel reference.
* With no true outlier, the lowest of $k$ leave-one-out means is still slightly below the true mean. It then flags a few more models high, which suits screening, where sensitivity matters more than specificity.

```{r loo_table}
purrr::map_dfr(runs, "models") |>
  left_join(select(purrr::map_dfr(runs, "summary"), joint, registry, p_re, loo_re_min), by = c("joint", "registry")) |>
  arrange(joint, registry, loo_re) |>
  transmute(joint = JOINT_NAME[joint], registry, `model left out` = model, `share of n` = pct(share_n, 1),
            `RE mean without it (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", pct(loo_re, 0.01), pct(loo_re_lb), pct(loo_re_ub)),
            `change from full RE mean` = pct(d_re, 0.01),
            `I2 without it` = paste0(round(I2_without), "%"),
            lowest = ifelse(abs(loo_re - loo_re_min) < 1e-12, "lowest", "")) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Random-effects mean without each model, ", T_YR, " years (metafor leave1out), sorted from lowest"))
```

```{r loo_plot, results = "asis", fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5.5}
for (j in names(runs)) {
  cat("\n\n### ", JOINT_NAME[[j]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- plot_loo_means(runs[[j]], methods = "loo_re",
         title = paste0(JOINT_NAME[[j]], ": random-effects mean without each model (", T_YR, " years)"),
         subtitle = "Grey band: published mean's 95% CI. Black line: published mean. Blue dashed: full random-effects mean",
         caption = "Purple: random-effects mean refitted without the model on the y axis (95% CI).")
  print(p); save_fig(p, paste0(tolower(j), "_", T_YR, "yr_loo_re"), 11, 5.5)
  src("<b>metafor output</b>: <code>leave1out(rma())</code>, drawn with ggplot2.")
}
```

# Influence diagnostics {#influence}

**Method.** `influence()` (metafor's `influence.rma.uni`) computes, for each model, how much the fit changes when that model is left out.

| Metric | What it is | How to read it |
|---|---|---|
| **Externally standardised residual** (`rstudent`) | $z_i = (y_i - \hat\mu_{(-i)}) / \sqrt{v_i + \hat\tau^2_{(-i)} + \text{Var}(\hat\mu_{(-i)})}$ | The model compared with the mean of all **other** models. Roughly N(0,1). See [below](#rstudent) |
| **DFFITS** | Change in the pooled estimate when model $i$ is removed, in standard-error units | Large \|DFFITS\|: removing the model shifts the mean noticeably |
| **Cook's distance** | Squared change in the pooled estimate when model $i$ is removed, scaled by its variance | Overall influence on the mean. metafor flags values above the median of $\chi^2_1$ (0.45) |
| **Covariance ratio** | Variance of the pooled estimate without model $i$ divided by with it | Below 1: removing the model makes the mean *more* precise, a sign of an outlier |
| **Hat value** | The model's leverage, its share of the weight | Above $3/k$: the model holds a lot of the estimate |
| **$\tau^2$ deleted** | $\tau^2$ refitted without model $i$ | A large drop: this model accounts for much of the heterogeneity |
| **Influential** | metafor's default flag (Viechtbauer & Cheung 2010) | Any of: \|DFFITS\| > $3\sqrt{1/(k-1)}$; Cook's > median $\chi^2_1$; hat > $3/k$; DFBETAS > 1 |

A model flagged **influential** is one that **drives the mean**: removing it changes the pooled estimate, its precision or the heterogeneity more than any of the other models.

```{r influence_table}
purrr::map_dfr(runs, "models") |>
  arrange(joint, registry, desc(n_total)) |>
  transmute(joint = JOINT_NAME[joint], registry, model, n = scales::comma(n_total), rate = pct(p),
            rstudent = num(rstudent), DFFITS = num(dffits), `Cook's D` = num(cook_d), `cov ratio` = num(cov_r),
            hat = num(hat), `tau2 deleted` = num(tau2_del, 3), influential = ifelse(influential, "YES", "")) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lllrrrrrrrrl", caption = paste0("Influence diagnostics, ", T_YR, " years (metafor influence)"))
```

```{r influence_native, results = "asis", fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7}
for (j in names(runs)) for (r in names(runs[[j]]$fits)) {
  cat("\n\n### ", JOINT_NAME[[j]], ", ", r, "\n\n", sep = "")
  plot(stats::influence(runs[[j]]$fits[[r]]$re))
  src("<b>metafor output</b>: <code>plot(influence(rma()))</code>. One panel per diagnostic; dashed lines are metafor's cut-offs, and influential models are shown in red.")
}
```

```{r cook, results = "asis", fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4.5}
for (j in names(runs)) {
  cat("\n\n### Cook's distance: ", JOINT_NAME[[j]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- plot_loo_cook(runs[[j]], title = paste0(JOINT_NAME[[j]], ": influence on the random-effects mean (", T_YR, " years)"))
  print(p); save_fig(p, paste0(tolower(j), "_", T_YR, "yr_cook"), 11, 4.5)
  src("<b>metafor output</b>: Cook's distance and influential flag from <code>influence()</code>, drawn with ggplot2.")
}
```

# Standardised residuals: the meta-analytic outlier test {#rstudent}

The externally standardised residual (`rstudent`) from `influence()` is an outlier test in its own right. It works without a funnel and scores each model by how far it sits from the **random-effects mean of the other models**, in standard-deviation units. It differs from a binomial funnel in three ways:

1. **It uses each model's published CI**, so it allows for censoring and the number still at risk. A funnel uses only n and assumes everyone was followed for the full time.
2. **It is leave-one-out by construction.** The model is compared with a mean built without it, so it cannot hide itself.
3. **It allows for genuine between-model variation ($\tau^2$).** It asks whether a model is unusual *given how much implants normally differ*, not whether it differs from the mean at all. It is the meta-analytic counterpart of an overdispersed funnel, and so it is more conservative.

Limits: ±1.645 (90%, solid) and ±1.96 (95%, dashed). A model flagged by both a funnel and this test is a strong signal. A model flagged only by the funnel is worse than the average, but within the normal spread between implants.

```{r rstudent_plot, results = "asis", fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5}
rs_all <- purrr::map_dfr(runs, ~ loo_rstudent_status(.x, P$summary_level))
plot_rs <- function(rs) {
  ggplot(rs, aes(x = n_total, y = rstudent)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.95), linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975), linewidth = 0.4, linetype = "22") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(aes(fill = status), shape = 21, size = 2.6, colour = "grey15", stroke = 0.3) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = model), size = 2.5, max.overlaps = Inf, seed = 1, min.segment.length = 0, colour = "grey30") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = LOO_STATUS_COLOURS, drop = FALSE, name = paste0("Status (", level_label(P$summary_level), ")")) +
    (if (P$x_log) scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) else scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma)) +
    facet_wrap(vars(registry), scales = "free_x") +
    labs(x = "Procedure volume (n)", y = "Leave-one-out standardised residual (z)") + theme_funnel()
}
for (j in names(runs)) {
  cat("\n\n### ", JOINT_NAME[[j]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- plot_rs(filter(rs_all, joint == j)) +
    labs(title = paste0(JOINT_NAME[[j]], ", ", T_YR, " years: leave-one-out standardised residuals"),
         subtitle = "Each model vs the random-effects mean of the other models. Solid: 90%; dashed: 95%")
  print(p); save_fig(p, paste0(tolower(j), "_", T_YR, "yr_rstudent"), 11, 5)
  src("<b>metafor output</b>: <code>rstudent</code> column of <code>influence(rma())</code>, drawn with ggplot2.")
}
```

# Control limits: Wald vs exact binomial {#limits}

*This section is not a metafor output. It compares the two ways of drawing funnel limits.*

* **Wald** (normal approximation): $p_0 \pm z\sqrt{p_0(1-p_0)/n}$. Symmetric, and simple to calculate and explain.
* **Exact binomial** (Spiegelhalter 2005): binomial quantiles, interpolated between whole counts. Asymmetric, and accurate at small n.

At low revision rates, the binomial distribution is skewed to the right, so the Wald upper limit is too low at small n and models are flagged high too often. The table shows how often each limit is exceeded by a model whose true rate *equals* the reference (5%), at the 90% level. The target is 5% on each side.

```{r calibration}
calib <- purrr::map_dfr(unlist(P$screen_levels), ~ limit_calibration(0.05, c(25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000), .x) |> mutate(level = .x))
calib |>
  transmute(level = level_label(level), n, method = METHOD_NAME[method], `upper limit` = pct(upper), `lower limit` = pct(lower, 0.01),
            `P(above upper)` = sprintf("%.3f", p_above), `x target` = sprintf("%.1f", p_above / target),
            target = sprintf("%.3f", target)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Real false-alarm rate of the upper limit for a true rate of 5% (binomial)")
```

The Wald limits are too liberal at small n: up to several times the target below n ≈ 250. The exact limits are never worse and are usually close to the target. Where both are equally off, the two limits fall between the same two whole counts; with discrete counts, no limit can hit the target exactly.

```{r limit_methods, results = "asis", fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5.5}
for (j in names(runs)) {
  cat("\n\n### ", JOINT_NAME[[j]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- plot_limit_methods(runs[[j]], P$summary_level, P$x_log,
         title = paste0(JOINT_NAME[[j]], ", ", T_YR, " years: Wald vs exact ", level_label(P$summary_level), " limits around the published mean"),
         subtitle = "Dashed orange: Wald (normal). Solid black: exact binomial")
  print(p); save_fig(p, paste0(tolower(j), "_", T_YR, "yr_wald_vs_exact"), 11, 5.5)
  src("Funnel limits from <code>R/limits.R</code> (not metafor).")
}
```

```{r wald_vs_exact_table}
purrr::map_dfr(runs, function(r) purrr::map_dfr(unlist(P$screen_levels), function(lv)
  bind_rows(mutate(loo_status(r, lv, "normal"), lim = "Wald"), mutate(loo_status(r, lv, "exact"), lim = "exact")))) |>
  filter(ref %in% c("pub", "min_loo_re")) |>
  select(joint, registry, model, n_total, p, ref, level, lim, status) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = lim, values_from = status) |>
  filter(Wald != exact) |>
  transmute(joint = JOINT_NAME[joint], registry, model, n = n_total, rate = pct(p),
            reference = LOO_REFS[as.character(ref)], level = level_label(level), Wald, exact) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Models whose status differs between Wald and exact limits (published mean and lowest leave-one-out mean; 90% and 95%)")
```

# 90% and 95% control limits {#screening}

**Why lower limits.** With the volumes typical of total elbows (100–500 per model), a 99.8% limit only flags implants that are dramatically worse. For screening, lower limits trade a few more false alarms for much better detection.

* A two-sided **90%** limit leaves 5% above the upper limit, so a high flag is a **one-sided test at α = 0.05**. This is the convention for non-inferiority, where a 90% CI is judged against a margin (den Broeder et al. 2023). 90% CIs are also used in orthopaedic cohort research (Groot et al. 2017).
* A **95%** limit is a one-sided test at α = 0.025.

**Power and false alarms.** For a reference rate of 5%, the table gives the probability that a model is flagged high, using `r METHOD_NAME[P$summary_method]` limits:

```{r power}
pw <- limit_power(0.05, c(1.5, 2, 3), c(50, 100, 250, 500, 1000), unlist(P$screen_levels), P$summary_method)
pw |>
  mutate(level = level_label(level), ratio = paste0(ratio, "x")) |>
  select(n, level, ratio, power, false_alarm) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = ratio, values_from = power, names_prefix = "power, true rate ") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !n, ~ sprintf("%.2f", .x))) |>
  rename(`false alarm (true rate = reference)` = false_alarm) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Probability of a high flag, reference rate 5% (", METHOD_NAME[P$summary_method], " limits)"))
```

**Funnels.** Each figure shows the 90% and 95% limits around two references: the **published mean** (top) and the **lowest random-effects leave-one-out mean** (bottom; from metafor `leave1out()`). Points are coloured by the strictest limit they are outside. Both Wald and exact versions are shown.

```{r screen_funnels, results = "asis", fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8}
SL <- unlist(P$screen_levels)
screen_by_method <- list()
for (m in c("normal", "exact")) {
  screen_by_method[[m]] <- purrr::map_dfr(runs, ~ screen_status(.x, SL, c("pub", "min_loo_re"), m))
  for (j in names(runs)) {
    cat("\n\n### ", JOINT_NAME[[j]], ", ", METHOD_NAME[[m]], " limits\n\n", sep = "")
    p <- plot_screen_funnels(filter(screen_by_method[[m]], joint == j), runs[[j]], SL, m, P$x_log,
           title = paste0(JOINT_NAME[[j]], ", ", T_YR, " years: 90% and 95% funnels (", METHOD_NAME[[m]], ")"),
           subtitle = "Top: published mean. Bottom: lowest random-effects leave-one-out mean (least upward-biased)",
           caption = "Labelled: models outside at least the 90% limit.")
    print(p); save_fig(p, paste0(tolower(j), "_", T_YR, "yr_screen_", m), 11, 8)
    src("Funnel limits from <code>R/limits.R</code>. The bottom row's reference is the lowest mean from <b>metafor</b> <code>leave1out()</code>.")
  }
}
```

```{r screen_counts}
purrr::imap_dfr(screen_by_method, function(ss, m) ss |>
  tidyr::crossing(level = SL) |>
  group_by(joint, registry, ref, level) |>
  summarise(models = n(), high = sum(!is.na(above) & above >= level), low = sum(!is.na(below) & below >= level),
            `flagged high` = paste(sort(model[!is.na(above) & above >= level]), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(limits = METHOD_NAME[m])) |>
  mutate(joint = JOINT_NAME[joint], reference = LOO_REFS[as.character(ref)], level = level_label(level)) |>
  arrange(joint, registry, limits, reference, level) |>
  select(joint, registry, limits, reference, level, models, high, low, `flagged high`) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Models above / below the limit, by limits, reference and level")
```

# Sensitivity: complementary log-log vs logit scale {#scale-sensitivity}

```{r scale_cmp, include = isTRUE(P$scale_compare), eval = isTRUE(P$scale_compare)}
SCALE_CMP <- loo_scale_compare(exts, cfg, unlist(P$time_yrs), scales = c(P$ma_scale, SC_OTHER), k_min = P$k_min,
                               test = P$ma_test, level = P$summary_level, method = P$summary_method)
SCALE_W <- loo_scale_wide(SCALE_CMP, P$ma_scale, SC_OTHER)
```

The whole analysis was refitted on the `r MA_SCALES[[SC_OTHER]]$label` scale, with the SE taken from the same published CIs on that scale. The table compares the two scales at each follow-up year: the random-effects mean, the lowest leave-one-out mean and the model it leaves out, and the models flagged against the lowest leave-one-out mean (`r level_label(P$summary_level)`, `r METHOD_NAME[[P$summary_method]]` limits). $\tau^2$ is on each scale's own units and is not comparable between rows.

```{r scale_table, eval = isTRUE(P$scale_compare)}
SCALE_CMP |>
  arrange(joint, registry, time_yr, factor(scale, levels = c(P$ma_scale, SC_OTHER))) |>
  transmute(joint = JOINT_NAME[joint], registry, years = time_yr, scale, k,
            `RE mean (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", pct(p_re, 0.01), pct(p_re_lb), pct(p_re_ub)),
            `95% prediction interval` = sprintf("%s-%s", pct(pi_lb), pct(pi_ub)),
            tau2 = num(tau2, 3), I2 = paste0(round(I2), "%"),
            `lowest LOO mean` = pct(loo_re_min, 0.01), `left out` = drop_for_min_re,
            `flagged vs lowest LOO` = ifelse(flagged == "", "none", flagged)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Random-effects results on the two scales, by follow-up year (metafor rma, leave1out)")
```

```{r scale_agree, results = "asis", eval = isTRUE(P$scale_compare)}
cat("\n\n**Agreement.** Across ", nrow(SCALE_W), " registry-by-year fits, the random-effects means differ by at most ",
    sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(SCALE_W$d_re_pp))), " percentage points and the lowest leave-one-out means by at most ",
    sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(SCALE_W$d_loo_pp))), " points. The same model gives the lowest leave-one-out mean in ",
    sum(SCALE_W$same_drop), " of ", nrow(SCALE_W), " fits, and the same models are flagged in ",
    sum(SCALE_W$same_flags), " of ", nrow(SCALE_W), ".", sep = "")
dis <- dplyr::filter(SCALE_W, !same_drop | !same_flags)
if (nrow(dis)) {
  cat(" Where they differ:\n\n")
  none <- function(x) ifelse(x == "", "none", x)
  flag_txt <- ifelse(dis$same_flags, "; flags identical",
                     paste0("; flags ", none(dis$flagged_a), " vs ", none(dis$flagged_b)))
  cat(paste0("* ", JOINT_NAME[dis$joint], " ", dis$registry, ", ", dis$time_yr, " years: lowest LOO leaves out ",
             dis$drop_for_min_re_a, " (", pct(dis$loo_re_min_a, 0.01), ", ", P$ma_scale, ") vs ",
             dis$drop_for_min_re_b, " (", pct(dis$loo_re_min_b, 0.01), ", ", SC_OTHER, ")", flag_txt),
      collapse = "\n")
  cat("\n\n")
} else cat("\n\n")
cat("Differences between the scales are small next to the width of the control limits, so the choice of scale does not change the conclusions where the flags agree. Where they differ, the two candidate means are close, and the model is borderline on either scale.\n\n")
```

# Summary {#summary}

```{r summary_data}
SUM_LV <- P$summary_level; SUM_M <- P$summary_method
summ <- purrr::map_dfr(runs, "summary")
mods <- purrr::map_dfr(runs, "models")
st <- purrr::map_dfr(runs, ~ loo_status(.x, SUM_LV, SUM_M)) |> filter(ref %in% c("pub", "min_loo_re"))
flag_list <- function(x) if (length(x)) paste(sort(x), collapse = ", ") else "none"
out <- st |>
  group_by(joint, registry) |>
  summarise(
    high_pub = list(model[ref == "pub" & status == "above"]), high_min = list(model[ref == "min_loo_re" & status == "above"]),
    low_pub  = list(model[ref == "pub" & status == "below"]), low_min  = list(model[ref == "min_loo_re" & status == "below"]),
    .groups = "drop")
drivers <- mods |>
  group_by(joint, registry) |>
  summarise(infl_names = flag_list(model[influential]),
            infl_detail = if (any(influential)) paste(sprintf("%s (Cook's D %.2f; mean without it %s; pulls the mean %s)", model[influential],
                                                              cook_d[influential], pct(loo_re[influential], 0.01),
                                                              ifelse(d_re[influential] > 0, "down", "up")), collapse = "; ") else "none",
            .groups = "drop")
S <- summ |>
  left_join(drivers, by = c("joint", "registry")) |>
  left_join(out, by = c("joint", "registry")) |>
  left_join(mods |> group_by(joint, registry) |> slice_min(loo_re, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
              select(joint, registry, min_lb = loo_re_lb, min_ub = loo_re_ub), by = c("joint", "registry"))
```

The summary uses **`r level_label(SUM_LV)` `r METHOD_NAME[SUM_M]` limits** and compares the published registry mean with the lowest random-effects leave-one-out mean, at **`r T_YR` years**.

## 1. Models driving the mean

```{r summary_drivers}
S |>
  transmute(joint = JOINT_NAME[joint], registry, k,
            `influential models (metafor)` = infl_detail,
            `model whose removal lowers the mean most` = drop_for_min_re,
            `full RE mean` = pct(p_re, 0.01)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Models that drive the random-effects mean (metafor influence and leave1out)")
```

```{r summary_drivers_text, results = "asis"}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(S))) {
  s <- S[i, ]
  cat("* **", JOINT_NAME[[s$joint]], ", ", s$registry, ":** ",
      if (s$infl_names == "none") "no model is flagged as influential by metafor's rule. " else
        paste0(s$infl_names, if (grepl(",", s$infl_names)) " are" else " is", " flagged as influential (driving the mean). "),
      "Leaving out ", s$drop_for_min_re, " gives the lowest mean (", pct(s$loo_re_min, 0.01), " vs the full RE mean of ",
      pct(s$p_re, 0.01), " and the published mean of ", pct(s$p_pub, 0.01), ").\n", sep = "")
}
```

An influential model can pull the mean **up** (a high-rate model, the masking case) or **down** (a large low-rate model, which makes the other models look worse). The least-biased mean removes the strongest *upward* pull, so it is obtained by leaving out the model in the "lowers the mean most" column, which is not always the model flagged as influential.

## 2. The least-biased mean to use

```{r summary_mean}
S |>
  transmute(joint = JOINT_NAME[joint], registry,
            `published mean (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", pct(p_pub, 0.01), pct(p_lcl), pct(p_ucl)),
            `RE mean (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", pct(p_re, 0.01), pct(p_re_lb), pct(p_re_ub)),
            `recommended: lowest RE leave-one-out mean (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", pct(loo_re_min, 0.01), pct(min_lb), pct(min_ub)),
            `obtained by leaving out` = drop_for_min_re,
            `difference from published` = pct(loo_re_min - p_pub, 0.01)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Least upward-biased mean for the funnel reference, ", T_YR, " years"))
```

## 3. Outliers: published mean vs lowest leave-one-out mean

```{r summary_outliers}
S |>
  rowwise() |>
  transmute(joint = JOINT_NAME[joint], registry, models = k,
            `high vs published (n)` = length(high_pub), `high vs published` = flag_list(high_pub),
            `high vs lowest LOO (n)` = length(high_min), `high vs lowest LOO` = flag_list(high_min),
            `newly flagged high` = flag_list(setdiff(high_min, high_pub)),
            `no longer flagged high` = flag_list(setdiff(high_pub, high_min)),
            `low vs published` = flag_list(low_pub), `low vs lowest LOO` = flag_list(low_min)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Outliers at the ", level_label(SUM_LV), " ", METHOD_NAME[SUM_M], " limit, ", T_YR, " years"))
```

```{r summary_outliers_text, results = "asis"}
tot_pub <- sum(lengths(S$high_pub)); tot_min <- sum(lengths(S$high_min))
cat("Across all registries and both joints, **", tot_pub, "** model(s) are above the ", level_label(SUM_LV), " ", METHOD_NAME[SUM_M],
    " upper limit against the published mean, and **", tot_min, "** against the lowest random-effects leave-one-out mean.\n\n", sep = "")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(S))) {
  s <- S[i, ]
  hp <- s$high_pub[[1]]; hm <- s$high_min[[1]]; new <- setdiff(hm, hp); gone <- setdiff(hp, hm)
  cat("* **", JOINT_NAME[[s$joint]], ", ", s$registry, ":** ", length(hp), " high vs the published mean (", flag_list(hp), "); ",
      length(hm), " high vs the lowest leave-one-out mean (", flag_list(hm), ").",
      if (length(new)) paste0(" Newly flagged: ", flag_list(new), ".") else " No new high outliers.",
      if (length(gone)) paste0(" No longer flagged: ", flag_list(gone), ".") else "", "\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r summary_rstudent, results = "asis"}
rs_flag <- rs_all |> filter(status != "within")
cat("\n\n**Meta-analytic check** (`rstudent`, ", level_label(P$summary_level), "): ",
    if (nrow(rs_flag)) paste(sprintf("%s %s %s (z = %.2f, %s)", JOINT_NAME[rs_flag$joint], rs_flag$registry, rs_flag$model, rs_flag$rstudent,
                                     ifelse(rs_flag$status == "above", "high", "low")), collapse = "; ") else "no model is unusual",
    ". Models flagged high by the funnel but not by this test are worse than the average, but within the normal spread between implants.\n", sep = "")
```

## Interpretation

* A model **flagged high against both references** is the strongest funnel signal. A model **newly flagged** against the lowest leave-one-out mean is one the published mean may have been hiding (masking). It is a screening signal worth reviewing, not a finding.
* The lowest leave-one-out mean is the recommended funnel reference for registries with few models (supervisor guidance). It is deliberately conservative, slightly low when there is no outlier.
* With $k$ = 4–5 (elbow), $\tau^2$ and the influence statistics are imprecise. Treat elbow results as illustrative.
* At 90%, about 1 in 10–20 models that perform like the reference is flagged high by chance (see the power table). Flags are hypotheses for review.
